qna.value:
What does it mean for you to fight for the UFC? To fight in the UFC is my dream and has been my dream since childhood, but now that I achieved this dream my next dream is to become a UFC Champion.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I used to watch fights with my father since I was a child and I always used to think to myself as a kid that when I grow up I will become a fighter. I also used to fight in the street a lot growing up so it was a no brainer to become a fighter lol.

Who is your favorite fighter and why? My favorite fighter is Jon Jones, I love the way he controls his opponents inside the cage and his fight IQ is out of this world.

Specific accomplishments in pro competition? I’m a 5 time Kickboxing Champion in Georgia. 2 time Boxing National Champion.

What fight do you consider to be the key fight in your career and why?  I think my fight on the Contender Series, it was a Split decision loss which I thought I didn’t lose and if you watch Dana’s interview after my fight even Dana White said he didn’t think I lost. Bit it is what it is and it was my first professional lost and I learned a lot from that fight.

Is there a cause that you want to use your platform for? I want to use my platform to let the fans and everyone know that nothing is impossible and if you work hard you can achieve anything you want.

Beyond a championship or money, what motivates you? My family motivates me before anything else and after that my country, I know that if I focus and work hard I can change many peoples lives and I will do that.

What was your job before you started fighting? No I never worked, I always trained and my father helped me achieve my dream.

Favorite grappling technique: Triangle Choke

Favorite Striking technique: Left liver kick

Tell us about your life outside of fighting: I have 2 daughters, I love them very much. My hobby is riding my horse all the way to the top of the mountain, this is the first thing I will do after I win my fight and go home to Georgia the next day.

What ranks and titles have you held? Brown belt in BJJ (Rafaello Oliveira), black band in KMAA’s homemade MMA style.

Do you have any heroes? My mother and father.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I received my bachelors degree in Sociology from the University of Tennessee.

What was your job before you started fighting? Student

Favorite grappling technique: Guillotine

Favorite Striking technique: High kick and superman punch.

“I’m doing a lot of sparring. A lot of ground grappling . Pat’s regular stable of top fighters include Matt Hughes, Jens Pulver, and Jeremy Horn to name a few. "It’s going great. They are tough guys. Usually our toughest fights are in our room" Pat says that he is doing more explosive, plyometric type training for this fight.

UFC History

Pat made his UFC debut in the UFC’s first ever under 170 pound tournament at UFC 16, "Battle in the Bayou". He defeated Olympic Silver Medal wrestler, Townsend Saunders, by a close decision and then defeated alternate Chris Brennan by submission to win the tournament. He was supposed to fight Lion’s Den fighter Mike Burnett in the finals but Burnett had to withdraw due to a hand injury. Pat fought Burnett at Ultimate Brazil to determine the first UFC Lightweight World Champion and won a split decision.

At UFC 18 Pat defended his title against Brazil's Jorge Patino. Patino had a reputation as a fearless fighter but choose to run away from Miletich for the majority of the fight. When the fight would go to the ground, Miletich easily got back up, looking for a knockout blow, but Patino would just start running away in circles again. Miletich remained undefeated in the UFC when all three judges gave him the decision.

Most of this match was spent on the feet exchanging punches and a few leg kicks, as well as the occasional clinch. Miletich got the better of the punching. In the second round Pederneiras threw a leg kick that was countered by a straight right hand of Miletich. The punch opened a cut over Pederneiras' eye. After a clinch Pederneiras pulled Pat down into his open guard but Pat just stood up out of it. When Pederneiras stood up he was bleeding profusely so referee John McCarthy brought him over for the doctor to check him out. The devastating quickness and power Miletich displayed against the formidable Carter only highlighted the remarkable achievement of his conqueror Newton. It was difficult to believe anyone could withstand the technical perfection and unyielding pressure that composes the fighting style of Miletich.

I've been with a new personal trainer three days a week, Matt Miller with Horsepower Strength and Conditioning, who has helped me improve my power, explosiveness, and overall strength by huge amounts. I've been doing heated power yoga three times per week. I've also been training at several different gyms with many tough training partners five times per week.

Biggest difference in training for this fight? The biggest difference is my desire to show my skills to a new audience and accomplish great feats in the UFC that haven't been done yet.

When and why did you start training for fighting? Ever since I was ten years old. Me and my brother used to fight a lot at home and our father thought it would be a good idea to put us in BJJ classes to control our temper. It only made the fights more technical (laughs). We soon started training kickboxing and the transition to MMA was natural. We were fans of the UFC since much younger; we saw Royce (Gracie) fight and were thrilled by it. Back then, the UFC and PRIDE were our passion. 

What professional titles have you held? I was the Bellator MMA Featherweight Champion three times. The first time I defended my belt twice, the second time I defended it five times and on the third time I had two title defenses before I left the promotion. I was also the Bellator MMA Lightweight Champion from May 2019 to November 2021. But due to the pandemic and issues with the promotion's schedule, I never defended that title. Meanwhile, my brother Patricky became the number one contender, so I vacated the belt and he won it after. Overall, I had 17 title fights and won 13 of them. I also won two Bellator Featherweight tournaments.

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? I have multiple regional titles in BJJ, also a Brazilian championship. My family couldn't afford to send me to world championships so that's as far as I could go back then.

TRAINING : A typical day of training usually involves pairing an hour and a half of BJJ with an hour and a half of either Muay Thai, MMA, or conditioning.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training for fighting once I became proficient in BJJ. I was training with Team Bison, which is very MMA oriented. Initially, I went there for the grappling, but quickly became involved in the fight game. I have since moved to Madison, where I continue to train MMA, BJJ, Muay Thai, etc. with Twisted Fitness.


What ranks and titles have you held? I have a BJJ Purple belt. I have also held the UCS 185-pound title.


Do you have any heroes? Socrates


What is your favorite technique? The Banana Split.


What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? The UFC represents the pinnacle of achievement in the fight game; it's such an honor to be a part of it.


Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? In undergrad I studied math with minors in physics and studio art. I am currently pursuing a masters in structural engineering at UW-Madison.


What was your job before you started fighting? I ran a painting business for five years. I'm also a researcher for the structural engineering department at the University of Wisconsin.
